title: Universal curve-test datum for a failure
statement:
Let $f:X\to S$ be affine and smooth of relative dimension one with $X$
affine, let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring, let $n$ be an integer
invertible on $S$ with $n\Lambda=0$, and let $q\ge1$. If
$\mathrm{BC}(f,\Lambda,q')$ holds universally for all $q'\le q-1$ but
$\mathrm{BC}(f,\Lambda,q)$ does not hold ([sk-def-bc]), then
there is a universal curve-test datum: a morphism $S'\to S$ and a
Cartesian square

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
X'=X\times_SS' & \xleftarrow{\;h\;} & Y\\
f'\downarrow & & \downarrow e\\
S' & \xleftarrow{\;g\;} & \Spec K
\end{array}
$$

with $S'=\Spec A$ affine, integral, normal, fraction field $L$
algebraically closed, $K/L$ an extension of algebraically closed
fields and $g$ the corresponding geometric generic point, $f'$ the base
change of $f$ (so affine and smooth of relative dimension one), and an
integer $d\mid n$, invertible on $S'$, such that

$$
R^qh_*(\Lambda/d\Lambda)\ \neq\ 0 .
$$

proof.text: Apply [sk-lem-failure-field] with the given $\Lambda$ and $q$. Its lower-degree universal hypothesis is exactly the hypothesis here. Obtain an affine $S_1$, a base change $f_1:X_1\to S_1$, a field $K_0$, $g_0:\operatorname{Spec}K_0\to S_1$, and a $\Lambda$-module sheaf $F_0$ for which the degree-$q$ arrow is not an isomorphism. Both $S_1$ and $\operatorname{Spec}K_0$ are qcqs by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]; [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1) makes $g_0$ qcqs. By universality [sk-def-bc], $\mathrm{BC}(f_1,\Lambda,q-1)$ holds. No assertion about all $\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z$-module sheaves is inferred from the hypothesis about $\Lambda$.

source.place: Tag 0F08, lemma-base-change-does-not-hold, proof; arbitrary-Lambda version of the current blueprint sk-lem-universal-datum

proof.text: Choose an algebraic closure $K$ of $K_0$ using [def-weil-algebraic-closure], and let $\rho:\operatorname{Spec}K\to\operatorname{Spec}K_0$. Each element of the algebraic extension satisfies a monic equation after division by its nonzero leading coefficient, so $\rho$ is integral by [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Both spectra consist of one point, so $\rho$ is surjective. Pull back the square and set $F=\rho^{-1}F_0$. Apply [lem-sbc-module-bc-integral-surjective] to $p=f_1$, $g=g_0$, and $\pi=\rho$. An isomorphism for $g_0\circ\rho,F$ would force one for $g_0,F_0$, contradicting Step 1. Thus the failure persists over the algebraically closed field $K$.

source.place: Tag 0F08, lemma-base-change-does-not-hold, proof; arbitrary-Lambda version of the current blueprint sk-lem-universal-datum

proof.text: Apply [lem-sbc-normalization-algclosed-field] to $g_0\circ\rho:\operatorname{Spec}K\to S_1$. This supplies an integral $\pi:S'\to S_1$, an affine integral normal $S'$ with algebraically closed function field $L$, and an embedding $L\hookrightarrow K$ inducing $g:\operatorname{Spec}K\to S'$ with $\pi\circ g=g_0\circ\rho$. Put $X'=X_1\times_{S_1}S'$ and $Y=X'\times_{S'}\operatorname{Spec}K$, with $f',h,e$ the projections. The squares paste to a base change of the original $f$. The affine-scheme and qcqs-permanence nodes show that $g$ is qcqs. To prove failure survives, suppose its new $\Lambda$-linear arrow were an isomorphism. By [lem-weil-pbc-exchange-forget-coefficients](1)-(3), forgetting scalars and taking degree-$q$ cohomology identifies it with the abelian base-change arrow; the forgetful functor is exact, so these are identifications of the arrows, not just their endpoints. The new abelian arrow would be an isomorphism. Apply [lem-sbc-integral-pushforward-base-change-arrow] with $\pi$ and $g'=g$: it makes the pasted abelian arrow an isomorphism. The same coefficient comparisons identify this with the underlying arrow from Step 2. A bijective $\Lambda$-linear map has a $\Lambda$-linear inverse sectionwise, so forgetting scalars reflects isomorphisms. The Step-2 arrow would therefore be an isomorphism, a contradiction. Only the implication from the new arrow to the pasted arrow is used; no conservativity of integral pushforward is needed.

source.place: Tag 0F08, lemma-base-change-does-not-hold, proof; arbitrary-Lambda version of the current blueprint sk-lem-universal-datum

proof.text: Every further base change of $f'$ is a base change of $f$ (paste its Cartesian square with those already constructed). Thus [sk-def-bc] gives $\mathrm{BC}(f',\Lambda,q-1)$. Apply [lem-sbc-module-bc-injectivity] to the qcqs $g$ and $F$. The degree-$q$ map is a monomorphism but not an isomorphism, hence $R^qh_*e^{-1}F\ne0$: a monomorphism with zero target has zero source and would be an isomorphism between zero objects. The map $h$ is qcqs by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](3), since it is a base change of $g$. It is not being identified with a base change of $f$.

source.place: Tag 0F08, lemma-base-change-does-not-hold, proof; arbitrary-Lambda version of the current blueprint sk-lem-universal-datum

proof.text: The composite $\operatorname{Spec}K\to S$ pulls the unit $n$ to a unit of the nonzero field $K$, so $n\ne0$. If the integer $n$ is negative, put $N=|n|$; then $N>0$, $N\Lambda=0$, and $N$ is invertible on $S$. (If $n$ is already natural this is just $N=n$.) The target in Step 4 is exactly $H^q(Rh_*Le^*(F[0]))$ of [sbc-def-base-change-map]: inverse image is exact for the constant coefficient ring. Apply [lem-sbc-prime-cyclic-detection] to $\Lambda,K,e,h,N,q,F$. Its hypotheses are now all established: $K$ is algebraically closed, $h$ is qcqs, $N\ne0$, and $N=0$ in $\Lambda$. It supplies a prime $r\mid N$ which is not a unit in $\Lambda$, and nonzero $R^qh_*\underline{P_r/(r)}$, where $P_r=\operatorname{ULift}(\mathbf F_r)$. This uses the existing arbitrary-coefficient devissage, and does not decompose a $\Lambda$-module into $\Lambda/d\Lambda$-summands.

source.place: Tag 0F08, lemma-base-change-does-not-hold, proof; arbitrary-Lambda version of the current blueprint sk-lem-universal-datum

proof.text: If $R^qh_*\underline{\Lambda/(r)}$ were zero, [lem-sbc-prime-quotient-detection], applied with the prime $r$ not a unit in $\Lambda$, would make $R^qh_*\underline{P_r/(r)}$ zero, contradicting Step 5. Thus $R^qh_*\underline{\Lambda/(r)}\ne0$. Set $d=r$. Since $r\mid |n|$, also $d\mid n$ in $\mathbf Z$. Pulling the unit $n$ back to $S'$ and writing $n=dt$ gives an inverse $t n^{-1}$ for $d$ in $\Gamma(S',\mathcal O_{S'})$. Hence $d$ is invertible on $S'$.

source.place: Tag 0F08, lemma-base-change-does-not-hold, proof; arbitrary-Lambda version of the current blueprint sk-lem-universal-datum

proof.text: Take $S'\to S$ to be the composite of the two base changes. Step 3 supplies its affineness, integrality, normality, the algebraically closed function field $L$, and the geometric generic point defined by $L\hookrightarrow K$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence](1), $f'$ is affine; by [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence](1), it is smooth of relative dimension one. Since $S'$ is affine, the same affine-permanence node also gives $X'$ affine if this is included in the datum. The Cartesian square and the nonzero higher direct image with the required $d$ are those of Steps 3 and 6. All the clauses of the original statement follow.

lean.note: Reuses upstream Etale.CurveTestDatum, constantModSheaf, higherDirectImage and BC properties.
